projects.name: Synapse
projects.tagline: Real-time collaborative whiteboard with live multiplayer drawing and conferencing
projects.description: Synapse is a full-stack collaborative whiteboard application enabling multiple users to draw, annotate, and communicate simultaneously. Built with PyQt6 for the native desktop UI, WebRTC for peer-to-peer media and data channels, and Python asyncio for the non-blocking signalling server. Features include infinite canvas, vector shape tools, sticky notes, voice/video chat, session recording, and end-to-end encrypted room codes.
highlights: Engineered a custom asyncio signalling server handling 500+ concurrent WebSocket connections
Implemented CRDT-based conflict resolution so concurrent edits never corrupt the shared canvas state
Reduced UI render latency to <16 ms by offloading canvas compositing to a QOpenGLWidget
Packaged as a single-file executable with PyInstaller for Windows, macOS, and Linux
projects.role: Solo developer – architecture, backend, frontend, DevOps

projects.name: Cattle Classify
projects.tagline: Transfer-learning CNN that identifies cattle breeds from farm photographs
projects.description: A 48-hour hackathon project that fine-tunes a ResNet50 backbone (pre-trained on ImageNet) to classify 14 cattle breeds from real-world farm photos. The pipeline covers data augmentation (random crop, flip, colour jitter), class-imbalance handling via weighted sampling, mixed-precision training with PyTorch AMP, and a lightweight FastAPI inference endpoint. Final accuracy of 91.3 % on a held-out test set beat the baseline VGG16 model by 7 pp.
projects.domain: Computer Vision, Machine Learning, Transfer Learning
highlights: Achieved 91.3 % top-1 accuracy by unfreezing only the last two ResNet50 residual blocks
Used Albumentations for 12-transform augmentation pipeline, cutting overfitting from 18 % to 4 %
Tracked 60+ experiments in Weights & Biases; identified optimal LR=3e-4 via sweep
Containerised inference server with Docker; cold-start latency under 400 ms on CPU

projects.name: PulseAPI
projects.tagline: High-throughput FastAPI microservice with Redis caching, JWT auth, and observability
projects.description: PulseAPI is a production-grade REST microservice template providing user authentication, rate limiting, and a pluggable business-logic layer. JWT access/refresh token pairs are issued at login; short-lived access tokens are validated in a dependency-injected middleware. Redis is used for distributed rate-limit counters and a read-through response cache that cuts database load by ~70 %. Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboards expose p50/p95/p99 latencies in real time.
highlights: Sustained 8 000 req/s on a 4-core machine using async SQLAlchemy and connection pooling
Redis cache cut average response time from 42 ms to 6 ms for read-heavy endpoints
Zero-downtime migrations via Alembic with blue-green deployment strategy
100 % test coverage on auth flows; fuzz-tested JWT edge cases with Hypothesis

projects.name: DataWeave
projects.tagline: Petabyte-scale Apache Spark ETL pipeline orchestrated on AWS EMR
projects.description: DataWeave is an enterprise ETL solution that ingests raw clickstream events from S3, applies multi-stage Spark transformations (deduplication, sessionisation, schema enforcement, PII masking), and writes partitioned Parquet to a data lake consumed by Redshift. Apache Airflow DAGs orchestrate daily and hourly runs; SNS alerts fire on SLA breach. The pipeline processes 2 TB of raw JSON per day with a wall-clock time of 23 minutes end-to-end.
highlights: Reduced daily ETL runtime from 4 h (legacy Hive) to 23 min via Spark adaptive query execution
PII masking stage achieves GDPR compliance without decrypting production data
Terraform modules provision a fresh EMR cluster per run, cutting idle cloud cost by 60 %
Backfill utility replays any date range idempotently using Airflow's catchup mechanism

projects.name: NeuralNotes
projects.tagline: LLM-powered study assistant that answers questions from your own uploaded notes
projects.description: NeuralNotes is a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) application that lets students upload lecture PDFs, slides, or plain-text notes and then chat with an AI that grounds every answer in the uploaded material. Documents are chunked, embedded with sentence-transformers, and stored in ChromaDB. At query time the top-k chunks are retrieved by cosine similarity and injected into a GPT-4o prompt, eliminating hallucinations about out-of-corpus content. A Streamlit frontend provides upload, chat, and citation-highlight UI.
highlights: RAG pipeline reduced hallucination rate from 34 % (vanilla GPT) to <3 % on domain-specific Q&A
Chunking strategy (512-token overlapping windows) improved retrieval precision by 18 % vs naive split
LangChain conversation memory preserves multi-turn context without exceeding context windows
Deployed to Streamlit Cloud; 400+ active users in first month

projects.name: ShiftScheduler
projects.tagline: React + Django SaaS for automated workforce scheduling and time-off management
projects.description: ShiftScheduler is a multi-tenant SaaS application used by retail and hospitality businesses to auto-generate weekly staff rosters, manage shift swaps, and track attendance. The Django REST Framework backend exposes a versioned API consumed by a React + TypeScript SPA. A constraint-satisfaction solver (Google OR-Tools) generates optimal schedules respecting labour law rules, employee preferences, and business demand forecasts. Stripe handles subscription billing; SendGrid delivers shift notifications.
highlights: OR-Tools solver generates a 50-employee week roster in <2 s, replacing 3 hours of manual scheduling
Multi-tenancy via row-level PostgreSQL schemas; zero cross-tenant data leakage verified by penetration test
Celery beat triggers nightly demand-forecast re-runs; staffing cost reduced by 12 % for pilot clients
Achieved SOC 2 Type I compliance; Stripe integration processes $40 k MRR
